principles: Closed test, not a public release: only invited testers; no public announcement; the landing does not promote pwa. during the tests; search engines are told not to index (TE-DQ-02).
Main targets, in this order: security, fault tolerance, stress (load) behaviour. Functional journeys are the vehicle for all three.
Measure, do not assume: each target has numeric exit criteria (exit_criteria) and a report.
Test data is test data: testers agree to the test terms; all data is reset before any public launch unless the owner decides otherwise (TE-DQ-11).
Third parties are out of scope for attacks and load: Neshan, the cPanel mail and landing host, the DNS provider, browser push services. Load against them is limited to what real journeys cause.
The contract stays at 1.5.0 during TE1; fixes that need a contract change wait for 1.6.0 unless they are security fixes.

CO-08 Community: read, react, post or comment where the contract allows (OQ-12 pre-moderation).
CO-09 Notifications: in-app and email; preferences; reminders.
CO-10 Privacy: consents on and off, data export (DSR) and account deletion.
CO-11 Help: file a support request, read the staff reply, get the solved notice (PB-04).
admin_console: AD-01 First staff sign-in: initial password, emailed code, new password, security key, recovery-code sheet (DQ-25, DQ-26).
AD-02 Second key, regenerate recovery codes, staff recovery with two ADM approvals, break glass on the server (drill).
AD-03 Four-eyes changes: policy publish, IRR rate change over 20 %, role grant, staff enable; Pending approvals duty (R-19).
AD-04 Daily IRR rate (morning notice, set today's rate).
AD-05 Moderation queues, case context, actions, removal awaiting ADM fairness approval (DQ-22).
AD-06 Verification queue of the demo providers: assign, request more info, approve, reject.
AD-07 Disputes with message threads; support inbox (assign, reply, close); DSR queue.

exit_criteria.note: Defaults; the owner confirms or changes them in TE-DQ-10. Each test edition ends with a report (T4.7, T5.8) that states the measured value next to each target.
functional: Every in-scope journey passes for at least 5 testers, in FA and EN, on Android Chrome and iOS Safari (PWA) and desktop Chrome or Edge (console).
No open severity 1 (data loss, security breach, total outage) or severity 2 (a journey blocked without a workaround) defect.
stress: Capacity measured, not assumed: the breaking point of the single backend process (step ramp until p95 > 2 s or errors > 2 %) is recorded with CPU, memory, event-loop lag and PostgreSQL figures.
Target load (default): 50 requests/s of the mixed journey profile for 30 minutes with p95 < 500 ms for reads, < 1000 ms for writes, error rate < 0.5 % (429 from rate limits counted separately).
Soak: 4 hours at 50 % of the target load with resident memory growth < 20 % and no rising latency trend.
Spike: 5x the target load for 2 minutes; the service recovers to target latency within 5 minutes without a restart.
Rate limits and PoW fire per visitor (after PB-12), not per server.
fault_tolerance: Every drill of T4.4 was run and its outcome recorded against its expected behaviour.
Recovery time (RTO) after a full server loss <= 4 h from the latest backup; data loss (RPO) <= 24 h (nightly backup) or the value the owner sets in TE-DQ-13.
No lost events: the outbox relays every event after a crash or restart; no media object without its database row and the other way round after a restore.
Restart behaviour is as decided in TE-DQ-01 (by default: everybody signed out, no data loss, service back within 60 s).
security: No open finding of high or critical severity; every medium finding triaged into fix-now, accepted-for-test (with a mitigation) or before-public-launch.
The pre-release security review (T1.13) and the tester campaign (T4.5) are recorded in a findings register with owner sign-off.
TLS and headers: A grade or better on testssl.sh; CSP with Trusted Types enforced on PWA and console; admin-api not reachable from outside.

release_gates.check: Backend, PWA and console pnpm check green; backend unit + integration + contract sweep green on a fresh database (or the two known failures waived with a reason); pnpm check:clients green; dependency audit without high or critical advisories.
Every te1_required item of P1 done; PWA builds and its unit tests pass; decisions TE-DQ-01..05 and TE-DQ-07..08 answered or defaults accepted.
The whole-plan strict test run (PD-03) green; a fresh-install rehearsal and a backup/restore rehearsal done with measured times; release candidate tagged.
Go/no-go: post-deploy smoke green on the server, security headers and TLS checked, staff signed in with keys, legal and consent texts published, owner checklist complete.
TE1 exit report accepted by the owner (exit_criteria), no open severity 1 or 2.
TE2 exit report accepted by the owner.

Rate limits behind the BFF: a trusted forwarded client IP (from the PWA, authenticated by its client assertion) or a confidential-client exemption on auth.signin/auth.token (PWA DI-25); per-caller buckets for cp-ssr server rendering (PWA DI-26) and a separate bucket for taxonomy.suggest typeahead (PWA DI-28).
Lower PoW difficulty for web sign-up or an up-front challenge hint in strict mode (PWA NI-P13-13, with the PWA).

notes.note_2026_11_19: Backend half done in BR-update-plan.json S26c.T2 (contract 1.5.0): SEC-WEB-3 Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site checks on POST /v1/auth/* (403 CSRF_FAILED; the synchronizer token is the interaction cookie binding, S26c-D3); X-Forwarded-For trusted from CARPAL_TRUSTED_PROXIES only; the signed BFF header CarPal-Forwarded-Client; ssr.read and ssr.search for cp-ssr without a forwarded visitor; RL(typeahead) for taxonomy.suggest; per-client PoW difficulty (not set by default). Open: the PWA and console BFFs must send CarPal-Forwarded-Client (pwa/BR-update-plan.json PB-12, console AC14b.T7); until then their calls count against 127.0.0.1 and backend.env keeps the raised IP windows. The up-front PoW solving is PWA work (PB-12).

assigned.note: Backend half done in S26c.T2; the rest is PWA PB-12 plus lowering the raised IP windows.

carried_items.title: Contract gaps raised by the PWA (PWA NI-P13-09, NI-P13-10, NI-P14-01..03)
text: Community: consumer posts (PWA DI-02), public member page (DI-03), saved posts/parts/searches (DI-06), followed_update cards with PublicOrgCard (DI-52) and organization name in the notification (DI-54), viewer context on community reads (DI-50), Q&A sort/node ids/follow/top answerers (DI-51), feed preferences (DI-31).

Public reads: slug history and redirects (DI-20), 410/merged_into (DI-37), a sitemap feed (DI-38), missing public fields (DI-39), public.org_get by id with locations, time zone and service modes (DI-60).

Account and auth: policy versions in config.client and optional consents at sign-up (DI-30), signals for locked accounts / remaining attempts (DI-33; suspended accounts stay generic, PWA OQ-17), session device labels and the first-factor AAL2 window (DI-56).

Garage and Help Me: free-text provider name and a light organization lookup (DI-47), sale date on StatusChange (DI-48), triage question options (DI-58), share_history on drafts and draft deletion (DI-61), triage.mine_list (DI-62), towing and region emergency numbers (DI-63), short appointment references (DI-64), appointment target for reports (DI-65).

Reviews and consents: review subject OrgSummary (DI-66), consent request caption/tags/needs-changes (DI-67), consents.requests_mine (DI-68), review appeals as moderation_appeal (DI-70); notification routes for answer-to-question, data-export-ready and request-received (DI-57).
Search and map: location time zone on ResultCard or PublicLocationPin (NI-P14-01), cluster members or pins with cluster_id (NI-P14-02), a separate highlight filter set on map.pins (NI-P14-03).
Fleet: IssueWrite.triage_session_id and the decision reason for drivers (DI-73); the fleet role model stays OQ-18 / NI-03 (PWA BA-22).

An E2E namespace or a cleanup command for the @test.carpal.app providers so earlier runs cannot skew rankings (PWA NI-P13-15).

text.issue: 42.db schema.md calls itself 'Doc 41 (db schema)' and calls the script '42.db_setup.sql'. 41.backend plan.md links '41.db schema.md' and '42.db_setup.sql'. The actual files are 42.db schema.md and 43.db_setup.sql, and the script header says 'Doc 42'.
text.action: Code and tooling use the real file names. Suggest the user renumbers the references in 41/42/43.

text.issue: Git tracks the folder as 'Docs/' but it appears as 'docs/' on this case-insensitive Windows disk.
text.action: Tooling must reference 'Docs/' exactly so it works on case-sensitive CI runners.

text.issue: 40 admin.assist_session_start says staff call allowlisted operations "through {adm}/assist/{assist_session_id}/… with the same bodies as the portal", but does not say how the "…" suffix maps to the portal paths (e.g. is org.update reached at {adm}/assist/{id}/orgs/{org_id}?). The registry carries the 20 allowlisted op ids (assistAllowlist) but no assist routes.
text.action: S8 decides the mapping (proposal: the portal path after /v1, e.g. /v1/admin/assist/{assist_session_id}/orgs/{org_id}) and the doc is corrected.

text.issue: 40 auth.authorize declares q: client_id: Str without bounds (every other Str has <a,b>). The generator accepts it as a non-empty single-line string.
text.action: Suggest Str<3,40> to match the CarPal-Client client_id rule (40 §1.3).

text.issue: core.normalize_search_text() uses lower() and the regex class \s, which follow the database ctype: under the default -v db_locale=C only ASCII letters are lower-cased and only ASCII whitespace is collapsed (checked in S2). With C.UTF-8 or ICU the same function lower-cases Unicode and collapses Unicode spaces.
text.action: libs/i18n normalizeSearchText takes the DB locale (CARPAL_DB_LOCALE) and matches either behaviour; an integration test compares it with the database. Suggest 43 pins the behaviour (e.g. lower(... COLLATE "und-x-icu") and an explicit space class) so search keys do not depend on the install locale.

text.issue: AAL2 is unreachable for accounts without a second factor, yet AAL2 guards the operations that enrol the first one (me.mfa_totp_enroll, me.webauthn_register_options) and everyday account operations (me.email_change, me.password_change, dsr.create, consent and onboarding operations). SEC-AU-10 defines aal2 as aal1 + second factor.
text.action: S3: a session records whether the account had an active second factor at sign-in (Session.mfaEnrolled); for sessions without one, a sign-in within the 10-minute step-up window satisfies AAL2 (re-authentication at the strongest level the account has). Staff, aal3 and enrolled accounts are unaffected. Suggest 40 SEC-AU-10 states this rule explicitly.

assigned.note: Also part of the security triage (AAL2 without a second factor).

text.issue: 40 declares no type for six non-Id path parameters: flow_type (onboarding.update/accept_terms, admin.onboarding_reset), slug (public.org_get), report_type (fleet.report), role (admin.platform_role_revoke), key (admin.flag_update), dashboard_key (admin.analytics_dashboard). The generator treated them as Id, which made those routes unreachable with real values.
text.action: Generator default table (UNTYPED_PATH_PARAMS): OnboardingProgress['flow_type'], Slug, FleetReportType, Role, Str<1,80>, DashboardKey. Suggest adding `param:` lines (like provider.gated_decide) to those blocks in 40.

text.issue: auth.password_reset_complete lists "422 VALIDATION_FAILED(breached_password)", but FieldErrorCode (40 §4.2) has no code for a breached password.
text.action: S3 answers VALIDATION_FAILED with { pointer: "/new_password" (or /password), code: "pattern" }. Suggest adding a FieldErrorCode such as "not_allowed" or "breached".

assigned.note: Also part of the security triage (breached-password field code, OQ-05).

text.issue: onboarding.update is ETAG (If-Match required), but a flow has no row, and so no version, before its first save.
text.action: S3: If-Match "v1" against a flow that does not exist yet creates it (version 1); any other version is 412. Suggest ETAG(if exists) for onboarding.update.

text.issue: 40 §6.2 does not say how the hosted sign-in UI returns to the client once AuthNext.next = "complete", and gives no error code for an unknown, expired or cookie-mismatched interaction_id.
text.action: S3: the hosted UI requests GET /oauth/authorize again with the same parameters; the __Host-cp_ia cookie names the completed interaction, so the server redirects to redirect_uri with code, state and iss (RFC 9207). Interaction errors are 410 LINK_EXPIRED (sign-in failures stay INVALID_CREDENTIALS). Suggest documenting both in 40 §6.2.

text.issue: me.email_change must not reveal whether the new address belongs to another account (202 always), so the conflict surfaces when the link is used; auth.email_verify lists only 410 errors.
text.action: S3: auth.email_verify answers 409 DUPLICATE when the new address was taken meanwhile (the link stays unused). Suggest adding "409 DUPLICATE" to auth.email_verify err.

text.issue: 52 §21 requires organization status active to publish a profile, but no operation of 40 moves an organization from draft to active (org.create must insert draft under RLS create_draft), and 56 §2.11 allows publishing with verification pending.
text.action: S4: provider.publish / vendor.publish activate a draft organization (draft|pending_verification|active may publish; suspended/archived/merged give organization_active in requirements). Suggest stating this in 40 provider.publish/vendor.publish and 52 §21.

text.issue: 52/40 do not say which default plan a hybrid_provider_vendor organization gets (billing plans have provider and vendor audiences only).
text.action: S4: hybrid starts on provider_basic (its public face is the provider profile); staff can reassign it. Product to confirm.

text.issue: Hybrid organizations: one membership per user and organization (role_memberships_org_uq), but {prv} routes need P* / P+ roles and {vnd} routes need V* / V+ roles, so the creator (provider_owner) cannot manage the vendor side; widening role groups is a contract change (40 §0.5).
text.action: Decide before the hybrid UI ships: e.g. in a hybrid organization provider_owner also satisfies V+/V* and vendor_owner P+/P*, or allow two memberships per user in hybrid organizations. S4 leaves the groups as written (workaround: invite a vendor_owner).

text.issue: 40 MediaAsset.status is 'active'|'quarantined'|'removed' but 52 MediaAsset has pending_upload, the state between upload_init and upload_complete.
text.action: S4: media.get answers 404 for pending_upload assets. Suggest adding pending_upload to MediaAsset.status in 40.

text.issue: 40 Url is https-only, but lite mode serves signed media URLs from the local http listener.
text.action: S4: the response check rewrites lite media URLs to an https placeholder (deviation); full mode uses the https media host. No contract change needed.

text.issue: 40 provider.coverage_create says each row is validated independently, but NodeId<type> checks (GD-17) run for the whole body in the pipeline, so one unknown node rejects the batch.
text.action: S4: parent chains and duplicates are per row (skipped codes); node existence/type is per request. Suggest 40 states that NodeId errors fail the whole request.

text.issue: S4 plan said provider.insights_get answers 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE until S9, but the operation has no FLAG and is not an AI feature; most of its figures belong to trust, appointment and analytics (S6-S8).
text.action: S4: implemented with this module's figures and 0/null from OrganizationExtensions.registerInsight until those modules register. Suggest marking which ProviderInsights/VendorInsights figures are nullable before their source exists.

text.issue: 40 HoursSpec day_of_week: Int<0,6> does not say which day is 0 (the pilot region's week starts on Saturday).
text.action: S4: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday (JavaScript getDay) in openNow. Suggest stating it in 40 §7.1.

text.issue: 40 OrgUpdate.slug allows at most 2 changes per 30 days, but no column records slug changes and no error code is named.
text.action: S4: counted in the KV store (30-day TTL), 429 RATE_LIMITED when exceeded. Suggest a slug_changed_at history (or audit read) and naming the code.

text.issue: 52 OrganizationLocation: exactly one primary per organization, but 40 LocationWrite.is_primary is a free boolean and does not say what happens to the first location or when the primary is deactivated.
text.action: S4: the first active location becomes primary; a second primary is 422 /is_primary not_unique; deactivating the primary promotes the oldest other active location, or 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(primary_location) when it is the only one.

text.issue: Maintenance reminders and document expiry need notifications (41 §6.3 hourly rule, Plan WP5), but 40 Appendix A / 50 §20 name no event for them; likewise no event when a stock-inquiry reservation expires.
text.action: S5 publishes vehicle.reminder.due (payload reminder_id via aggregate, vehicle_id, status due|overdue, reminder_type, owner_type, owner_id) when a reminder becomes due or overdue; reservation expiry publishes nothing yet. Suggest adding vehicle.reminder.due (and inquiry.reservation.expired if the requester should be told) to Appendix A and 50 §20 before S6 builds the notification consumers. S7 adds appointment.reminder.due the same way (DI-54).

text.issue: 40 §4.4 VIN_INVALID covers "format or check-digit rules", but the ISO 3779 check digit is mandatory only for North American (WMI 1-5) and Chinese (L) VINs; pilot-region VINs (WMI N*) use position 9 freely, so a strict check would refuse real vehicles.
text.action: S5: format always; check digit only for WMI 1-5 and L (modules/vehicle/domain/vin.ts). Suggest 52 §8 state the rule.

text.issue: vehicle_data_sharing is a personal consent (52 ConsentRecord: organization subjects only for the three *_ai_use types), but fleet vehicles belong to an organization: 40 does not say how a fleet shares documents or service history with a provider, or how a provider logs work on a fleet vehicle.
text.action: S5: a fleet shares its own documents by its coordinators' decision (FC role, no consent record); provider.service_record_create and job-log vehicle links fail closed (403 CONSENT_REQUIRED) for fleet vehicles. Needs a decision in S7/S8 (e.g. an organization-subject vehicle_data_sharing, or appointments as the only path for fleets). S7: fleet appointment requests ignore share_history (DI-58); providers record work on fleet vehicles through appointments (provider.service_record_create with appointment_id needs no consent).

text.issue: 52 VehicleIssue.description is 10–3000 characters; 40 IssueWrite.description is Text<3000> without a minimum.
text.action: S5: the 52 minimum is enforced by the use case (422 /description too_short, limit 10). Suggest Text<10,3000> in 40.

text.issue: 52 Vehicle.profile_completeness (S, 0–100) and InventoryItem.data_quality_score have no weights; 54 §7.2 lists the data-quality criteria only; 54 §3.2/§7.2 name inquiry_fulfillment_rate without a definition.
text.action: S5: equal weights (vehicle: 12 optional criteria + brand/model/year; item: images, part numbers, category, warranty note, description, stock status); inquiry_fulfillment_rate = share of the last 90 days' decidable inquiries the vendor answered within 24 h without marking them unavailable (requester cancellations before an answer and fresh unanswered ones excluded). See OQ-09 for the same question about profiles. S7: the vendor trust score uses the measured inquiry response time for inquiry responsiveness (54 §3.2) until inquiry_fulfillment_rate is defined.

text.issue: 40 ImportCreate.column_mapping.field is Str<1,60> with no list of target fields, and gives no way to name a part category other than its node id.
text.action: S5: fields are the InventoryItemWrite members with translations per locale (name_translations.en …; modules/inventory/domain/import-row.ts IMPORT_FIELDS); categories by node id only. Suggest an enum in 40 and a category-by-slug or label option (or the S9 AI classify_category).

text.issue: 40 vehicles.vin_reveal lists no error for a vehicle without a VIN; vin_decode uses 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(no_vin).
text.action: S5: vin_reveal answers 404 NOT_FOUND for a vehicle without a VIN. Suggest listing 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(no_vin) like vin_decode.

text.issue: InventoryItem.data_quality_score and the missing_images filter depend on image attachments, which the media module owns and changes without an event (media.attach / detach / delete).
text.action: S5: scores are recomputed on every item write, after imports and by the daily W15 rule inventory.catalog_quality; missing_images asks media per page. Suggest a media.attachment.changed event (or an attach hook through AttachmentTargets) so owning modules can react.

text.issue: 40 inquiries.vendor_get is CNS(vendor_fitment_context: for vehicle snapshot) without saying whether a missing consent refuses the read or hides the snapshot; 41 §6.3 says expired reservations are "released" without the target status.
text.action: S5: the inquiry is always readable by the vendor; the snapshot is null while the consent is missing or withdrawn (checked on every read). An expired reservation goes back to answered (still open) with reserved_until cleared.

text.issue: 40 Appendix A lacks events S6 needs: unpublication and vendor publication (only provider.profile.published exists), profile/location edits for the search indexer, community content changes, post publication for followers, reaction counts for counters other modules own, and the in-app security alert of SEC-AU-5.
text.action: S6 publishes provider.profile.unpublished, vendor.profile.published, vendor.profile.unpublished, organization.profile.updated {change: profile|location|organization}, community.content.changed {entity_type, entity_id}, community.post.published {organization_id, post_type}, community.reaction.changed {target_type, target_id, reaction_type, count} and user.security_alert {user_id, kind}; vendor.inventory.imported gained requested_by_user_id. Suggest adding them to Appendix A and 50 §20.

text.issue: 40 questions.update is ETAG but PublicQuestion carries no version, so a client cannot learn the value for If-Match.
text.action: S6: questions.create / get / update send the ETag header ("v<version>") even though the body has no version. Suggest adding version to PublicQuestion (author view) or dropping ETAG.

text.issue: 40 SearchMode has showcases and qna, but ResultCard.target is organization or inventory_item only; showcases and questions have their own reads (showcases.get, questions.search).
text.action: S6: search_mode showcases and qna rank providers like providers mode (the match session records the mode). Suggest dropping the two modes from SearchRequest or defining their result cards.

text.issue: 40 SearchRequest.issue_id links a search to a vehicle issue, but nothing says how it changes the search (symptom context, urgency) and the vehicle module exposes no issue read for other modules.
text.action: S6: issue_id is not stored or used (MatchSession.issue_id null); the urgency_level of the body and the safety check apply. S7 (Help Me / appointments from issues) should add a VehicleCards issue read and use the issue's symptom as a chip.

text.issue: answers.delete of an accepted answer: the answer's author may not change another user's question (RLS author_all), so the accepted reference cannot be cleared, and 40 names no error.
text.action: S6: deleting an accepted answer is 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(accepted_answer). Suggest either a definer that reopens the question or documenting the 409.

text.issue: notification.push_device_tokens.token_hash is unique across users, but a device that signs into another account registers the same token while the old row belongs to the previous user (invisible under RLS).
text.action: S6: the second account gets 409 DUPLICATE (/token not_unique); sign-out should revoke the token (push_tokens.revoke). Suggest a definer that moves the token to the new account, or revocation on session end (S9 hardening).

assigned.note: Push token revocation on sign-out comes with web push (TE2).

text.issue: 40 Appendix A lacks events S7 needs: appointment reminders, notes, delays and calendar changes, review edits/removals, response publication, invitation reminders, dispute opening and stock-inquiry status changes (requesters cannot be told about answers otherwise).
text.action: S7 publishes appointment.reminder.due, appointment.note_added, appointment.delay_reported, appointment.availability.changed, review.edited, review.removed, review.response.published, review.response.removed, review.invitation.reminded, dispute.opened and inquiry.status_changed with id-only payloads. Add them to Appendix A and 52 §20.

text.issue: 40 appointments.create names no error for the SEC-BF-3 open-request caps and the no-show cooldown, and no values for them.
text.action: S7 answers 429 RATE_LIMITED (retry-after 3600) at 3 open requests per provider, 10 in total, or within 7 days after a no-show at that provider (proposed values).

assigned.note: The open-request caps are checked in the security and abuse campaign.

text.issue: 52 §12 requires a capacity check at confirmation, but a provider without availability rules has no capacity defined; 40 does not say whether such providers can confirm.
text.action: S7: a location without any active rule has no calendar; confirmation checks only time off (same advisory lock) and public.availability offers no slots. Product to confirm.

text.issue: 40 Appointment.requester_contact is "for the requester's preferred channel", but in_app and push have no address and many users set no preference.
text.action: S7 (definer appointment.requester_contact): the verified email when the preference is email or unset, the verified phone for sms, otherwise null.

text.issue: 40 AppointmentCreate.share_history creates personal consents, but fleet requests have no personal consent subject for fleet vehicles (see DI-38).
text.action: S7 ignores share_history for fleet requests (consent_to_share_history false); decide with DI-38 / OQ-11.

text.issue: 40 review_responses.update says a published response is "re-moderated", but ReviewResponse has no moderation status.
text.action: S7 keeps an edited published response published; S8 moderation may add a status or a queue entry.

text.issue: 54 §9.4 publishes trust.score.changed only for changes above 5 points, but the search index (W2) needs every change to rank by the current score.
text.action: S7 publishes trust.score.changed on every change and audits only changes above 5 points (and the first score).

text.issue: 52 ProviderCapabilityEvidence.base_weight is an integer (smallint in 43), but 54 §1.1 review weights are fractional for Path 2 (8 × 0.6 = 4.8, 4 × 0.6 = 2.4).
text.action: S7 rounds (5 and 2). Change the column to numeric(5,2) in a numbered migration if calibration needs exact weights.

text.issue: 40 Appendix A lacks events S8 needs: feature_flag.changed (flag cache bust in every process), user.deletion.requested (approved deletion handed to the worker), dsr.deadline.approaching (staff alert); fleet.approval.requested from provider.appointments_update has no approval yet (the fleet decides by threshold).
text.action: S8 publishes them with id-only/plain payloads; fleet.approval.requested carries approval_id when an approval exists (W5 notifies only those). Add them to Appendix A and 52 §20.

text.issue: 52 Notification.event_type has no type for fleet approval decisions, DSR deadline alerts or verification outcomes.
text.action: S8 uses system_announcement (fleet decisions), moderation_alert (DSR deadlines) and moderation_update (moderation outcomes, verification, location corrections). Suggest fleet_approval_decided, dsr_deadline_alert and verification_decided in 52 and 43.

text.issue: 40 admin.analytics_dashboard takes region and organization_type filters, but 43 events.daily_metrics aggregates have a free dimension_key and 52 names no dimensions.
text.action: S8 stores aggregates without dimensions and ignores both filters. Decide the dimensions (region, org type, platform) before dashboards are used.

text.issue: 40 admin.dispute_resolve: for review_approval_objection, 52 §11 says an upheld objection publishes the review with disputed_by_business, i.e. 'upheld' means the review is upheld, not the business's objection.
text.action: S8 follows 52: resolved_upheld publishes (reviewer decision approved by the dispute decider, reason objection_upheld); resolved_rejected rejects the review. Suggest wording in 40 that names the outcome for the review explicitly.

text.issue: 43 media.media_assets.mime_type allows images, video, PDF and CSV only, so a DSR export bundle cannot be JSON.
text.action: S8 writes the bundle as one CSV in long format (section, record_id, field, value). Suggest allowing application/json (or zip) for system_export if a structured bundle is required.

text.question: Proposed entitlement values beyond max_vehicles and proposed retention periods (41 §10) are seeded as-is. Confirm before S8.

assigned.note: Confirm before TE1 (entitlements and retention periods apply to tester data).

text.question: Breached-password source for SEC-AU-7: a k-anonymity range service (e.g. Have I Been Pwned) in full mode, an offline list shipped with the backend, or both?
text.default_if_unanswered: Small built-in list in lite mode; full mode to be decided before production.

assigned.note: Security triage: breached-password source for the test.

text.question: Is Google/Apple sign-in (auth.social_start, SEC-AU-13) needed for the pilot region, and which provider credentials will be available?
text.default_if_unanswered: Deferred; password and one-time-code sign-in only.
text.follow_up: PM-01 in post_mvp_backlog. S9.T6 lists auth.social_start as deferred (reason: post-MVP, PM-01); the route keeps its 501 placeholder.

text.question: Community moderation in the MVP: may text without links or contact data go live at once (automated pre-moderation, GD-22), with reports and the S8 queue as the safety net, or must every post, comment, question and answer wait for a moderator?
text.default_if_unanswered: Automated pre-moderation as implemented in S6; links, emails and phone numbers wait for the queue.

assigned.note: Confirm before TE1: testers will post community content.

text.question: Default notification preferences (S6: in-app all but marketing; email and push for operational categories; community and AI suggestions in-app only; SMS off) and the digest schedule (daily = 24 h after the oldest pending item, weekly = 7 days).

assigned.note: Confirm before TE1.

text.question: Search defaults not fixed by 54: default radius (S6: 50 km, 25 km for the Discover feed), neutral scores without data (0.5), capability fit per confidence level (0.1 / 0.45 / 0.8 / 0.92 / 1.0) and rating trust weighting (full weight from 10 reviews).
text.default_if_unanswered: The S6 values, revisited when S7 adds trust scores and availability.

assigned.note: Confirm before TE1.

text.question: Fleet approval workflow: may fleet owners and managers book appointments without an approval while the workflow is on (S8 default), and should drivers be allowed to request appointments for their assigned vehicles?
text.default_if_unanswered: Owners/managers book freely; coordinators need an approved repair_request or provider_selection; drivers report issues only.

text.question: Moderation intake: should held content (links/contact data in community text and Path 1 reviews, public media, showcase items) open low-severity cases automatically (S8), or should moderators work from per-type queues instead?
text.default_if_unanswered: Automatic system_rule cases every 5 minutes, one per target.

assigned.note: Confirm before TE1: moderators work the queues during the test.

text.question: Which analytics dimensions should dashboards support (region, organization type, platform, entry point), and for how long may search.zero_result query text be kept?
text.default_if_unanswered: No dimensions; no query text in analytics events (only language and mode).

text.question: Fleet role model (RCP-03): which contract role is the "dispatching manager" (fleet_maintenance_coordinator, or a new role)? Should fleet_viewer stay organization-wide? Do operators and in-house mechanics become roles limited to linked vehicles, and may a vehicle be linked to several people (assignment kinds)?
text.default_if_unanswered: Contract as is: owner, manager, coordinator and viewer see the whole fleet; only fleet_driver is limited, one active assignment per vehicle, set by FC.

text.raw_text: Backend S26c.T2 (NI-19): the auth host checks Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site on POST /v1/auth/* (403 CSRF_FAILED), trusts X-Forwarded-For only from CARPAL_TRUSTED_PROXIES, and accepts a BFF visitor address in the optional signed header CarPal-Forwarded-Client (Docs/40 1.5.0 §1.3). taxonomy.suggest moved to its own bucket RL(typeahead); cp-ssr without the header uses ssr.read and ssr.search; per-client PoW difficulty CARPAL_POW_CLIENT_DIFFICULTY_BITS (not set by default).
text.proposal: (1) BFF forwarder (/api), the /id auth proxy and server rendering (cp-ssr): send CarPal-Forwarded-Client on every backend call made for a browser: a compact JWS signed with the client key of CARPAL_PWA_CLIENT_PRIVATE_JWKS (cp-web-consumer for /api and /id, cp-ssr for server rendering), header typ carpal-fwd+jwt, kid of the key; claims iss = sub = client_id, aud = the backend host URL (the issuer for /id, the API audience for /api), htm and htu of the upstream request (htu = aud + path, no query), cip = the visitor IP (from the X-Forwarded-For that nginx sets for the PWA, rightmost address, only when the PWA itself runs behind that nginx), iat, exp at most 60 s later. A key may sign one statement per visitor and URL per minute (cache), never a statement for another visitor. Keep stripping X-Forwarded-For. (2) No CSRF token is added on the auth routes: the backend binds them to the __Host-cp_ia interaction cookie (S26c-D3); keep forwarding Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site from the /id proxy. CSRF_FAILED from the backend is already handled as the BFF code.
